mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) as a continuous variable predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates reduce discount rates and boost equity valuations.
failure_condition: The correlation between FEDFUNDS level and 20-day forward returns is not significant (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window, or the direction of the relationship reverses in more than 50% of the data.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) falls below 3.0%, it signals an easing monetary policy that leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 3.0, or the Rank IC for the threshold condition is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of a federal funds rate below 3.0% and unemployment rate above 5.0% indicates a policy response to economic weakness, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 3.0 AND UNRATE > 5.0, or the Rank IC for the interaction condition is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS rising more than 0.3 percentage points over three months), S&P 500 forward returns are negative over the next 20 trading days due to reduced liquidity and growth concerns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises > 0.3pp in 3 months, or the Rank IC for the regime condition is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the unemployment rate (UNRATE) as a continuous variable predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as elevated unemployment signals economic distress and reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: The correlation between UNRATE level and 5-day forward returns is not significant (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window, or the direction of the relationship reverses in more than 50% of the data.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 5.0%, it indicates a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE > 5.0, or the Rank IC for the threshold condition is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of industrial production (INDPRO) above 120 and employment (PAYEMS) above 133000 indicates strong economic supply and labor conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: strong economic supply and labor conditions
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO > 120 AND PAYEMS > 133000, or the Rank IC for the interaction condition is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 2000.0), S&P 500 forward returns are positive over the next 60 trading days due to sustained economic growth and investor confidence.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where HOUST > 2000.0, or the Rank IC for the regime condition is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
